---
title: "Static formats"
subtitle: "What Veil does when there is no browser runtime."
description: "Learn how Veil removes hidden content at render time in PDF, Typst, Word, and other formats, and how it compares with conditional content."
---

## How it works

Only `html` and `revealjs` have the runtime.
In all other formats, `dashboard` included, Veil renders a static result from the resolved state.

- Veil removes each veiled element that is not visible in the resolved state.
- A removed header removes its section.
- Veil removes the class `.veil` and the attribute `group` from the elements that it keeps.
- Quarto then numbers sections, figures, and tables without gaps.
- Footnotes and citations that occur only in removed content do not show.

Set the state with the `state` option.
You can set it for one format only.
See [State and sharing](state.qmd#options-for-one-format).

## Compare with conditional content

In formats without the runtime, `.veil` is close to Quarto conditional content.

| | `.veil` | `.content-visible` and `.content-hidden` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chosen by | Group names and the state. | The format, or a metadata value. |
| Changes in the browser | Yes, in `html` and `revealjs`. | No. The choice is made at render time. |
| Several levels | Yes, with the ladder. | No. |
| Cross-reference to removed content | Veil writes a warning. | Quarto writes its own unresolved-reference warning. |
| Section numbers | Hidden sections keep their numbers in HTML. No gaps in static formats. | No gaps. |

: `.veil` compared with `.content-visible` and `.content-hidden`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[24,38,38]"}

Use `.content-visible` to change content by output format.
Use `.veil` to change content by audience.

## Numbers in HTML

In HTML, hidden sections keep their numbers and footnotes, because Quarto fixes HTML numbers at render time.
In static formats, the numbers have no gaps.

## Cross-references

A cross-reference to content that a `.veil` element removed gets a warning from Veil.
The element can be a section or a figure that carries `.veil`.
The warning gives the reference and the group, for example "`@sec-deep` points to content that the group `advanced` removed".
Quarto also writes its own unresolved-reference warning for the same reference.

A figure or a callout nested inside removed content gets only the unresolved-reference warning from Quarto.
Veil does not know about it, because the figure itself has no `.veil`.

## Limits

- Veil does not move the state to another page of a book or a website.
- Quarto search indexes hidden content in HTML.
